subject: Immediate approval request — reverse canary for model-Delta-12 due to memory-bleed tail latency
messages:
From: Caroline Holt <caroline@greenthread.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-29T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Significant tail latency and timeouts on /classify endpoint (model-Delta-12)

Sergio —

We're seeing a sudden jump in tail latency (p95 -> 1.8s, p99 -> 4.6s) and several 504 timeouts on our production /classify endpoint since the canary switched to model-Delta-12 this morning. Traffic is low but the impact is customer-visible (mobile app errors). Attached are short traces and the stack sample we captured.

Can you escalate? We need either an immediate rollback to model-Delta-11 or a temporary traffic cap while you investigate. Our SREs are standing by.

Caroline
Caroline Holt
Head of Platform Engineering — Greenthread AI

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-29T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Significant tail latency and timeouts on /classify endpoint (model-Delta-12) — request to reverse canary

Team — forwarding Greenthread's incident. Key points:
- Symptom: p99 latency spike and intermittent 504s on their prod canary (Delta-12).
- Customer asks for immediate rollback to Delta-11 or traffic cap.
- Attachments: short canary logs CSV + heap sample they gathered.

Initial triage from runtime: observed steady KV cache growth in the canary pod, correlated with long-tails and GC pressure (heap growth visible). This looks like a memory-leak/eviction edge-case in the Delta-12 KV cache handling under low but bursty traffic patterns.

Ask: I need explicit approval to reverse the canary (pin them back to Delta-11) and to authorize a temporary SLA carveout language for Greenthread while we stabilize (sales/lead to confirm wording). If approved, infra will run the rollback (canary -> previous stable) and monitor for 30 minutes before marking closed.

Attachments: canary-logs-20270529.csv, heap-growth-sample.txt

Sergio Alvarez
Account Lead — Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-29T13:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Significant tail latency and timeouts on /classify endpoint (model-Delta-12) — request to reverse canary

Thanks for the summary, Sergio. Quick technical note: runtime team sees KV cache growth tied to a new cache key normalization path introduced in Delta-12. Under certain TTL combinations the cache isn't trimming as expected which leads to transient GC spikes and long tail latencies. The behavior reproduces in canary.

Recommendation: approve immediate reversal to Delta-11 for Greenthread's canary. We should also add a short mitigation: reduce per-request KV retention window for the canary and push a patch to Delta-12 that hard-limits cache growth (non-blocking). If we reverse now we avoid a broader customer impact.

A couple of asks before I approve operationally:
- Confirm rollback runbook steps (who executes, who notifies customer)
- Confirm whether the revert touches their persisted data/chunks (I believe not, but legal should confirm)

Markus
Director, Runtime Engineering
[On-call: +1-555-RUNTIME]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-29T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reversal approval + customer-facing language

Short — sales/AM perspective: Greenthread is a mid-market account on committed Dedicated capacity (annual). They're sensitive to visible failures. If we revert the canary quickly and propose a limited SLA concession (one-week p95 credit or a one-time operational credit) that should preserve trust.

I don't want us to over-promise. Suggested language for customer outreach (we can tweak):
"We're authorizing an immediate canary reversal to the previously stable model (Delta-11) while our engineers push a patch to Delta-12. We'll monitor your traffic for 30 minutes and follow up with a RCA and remediation timeline. As a gesture, we're prepared to apply a one-time credit equivalent to 7 days of baseline inference spend if the regressions impacted production beyond the canary."

If legal/finance signs off, I'm good to coordinate communications.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
